fix: recover from poisoned preferences mutex

Replace .lock().unwrap() with .lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
in set_path_override() and path(). A panic in any thread holding
PATH_OVERRIDE would otherwise crash the TUI on the next preferences
access. Add a unit test that verifies the recovery pattern survives a
panicked lock holder.

fix: remove unreachable unwraps from containers render path

Replace app.container_state.as_mut().unwrap() and .as_ref().unwrap()
calls at the stateful widget render and action-in-progress blocks with
the existing state binding from the early-return guard at the top of
the function. NLL keeps the borrow live across the full function, so
the redundant re-access is unnecessary and the unwrap cannot panic any
more. Rename the shadowed state binding in the confirmation dialog
block to confirm_state for readability. Add render tests covering the
None, empty, loading, error, and action-in-progress code paths.

fix: replace unreachable in render paths with safe fallbacks

Three render/dispatch sites used unreachable!() for branches that are
logically impossible given earlier code but would crash the TUI if an
enum variant was added without updating the match, or if an early-return
guard was accidentally removed. Replace each with debug_assert! plus a
safe fallback:

- provider_list.rs: toggle fields return early if they reach the value
  match block
- tunnel_form.rs: Type field returns early in both the value and
  placeholder match blocks
- handler.rs zone_data_for: unknown provider returns empty slice pair,
  all call sites already tolerate empty iteration

Add exhaustiveness-guarded tests that iterate every ProviderFormField
and TunnelFormField variant through render_field_content, so a missing
early-return surfaces as a test failure rather than a runtime panic.
Add a happy-path test for zone_data_for covering all known providers.

- src/app/tests.rs (6415 lines): the existing #[cfg(test)] mod tests

app.rs keeps the App struct, impl Drop for App, impl App with all
behavior methods, and pub re-exports so external callers see the
existing API.

Include two performance fixes in apply_sort:
- AlphaAlias and AlphaHostname sort modes: replace sort_by with
  sort_by_cached_key and to_ascii_lowercase so each host's lowered
  key is allocated once per sort instead of twice per comparison.
- Group tab order dedup: replace the O(N^2) Vec::contains scan with
  a HashSet<&str> while preserving Vec ordering.

fix: drop unused DisplayTag re-export from app

DisplayTag is only constructed in types.rs and consumed by the test
module via super::*. The pub use re-export in app.rs made the binary
build warn about an unused import, even though cargo clippy --tests
stayed green because the test build exercised DisplayTag through
super::*. Drop the re-export and import DisplayTag explicitly in
app/tests.rs via super::types::DisplayTag.

refactor: split app.rs impl App into per-concern submodules

Cleaner Podman fleets, snappier containers, safer exec

Podman support broke for any host that returned array-shaped Names
or Ports (podman 5.x default), emitted an empty Status string, or
ran podman 3.x with its OomKilled field. The container listing
parser now accepts both shapes, the runtime relabels itself when a
docker-shim emits podman JSON, and the state glyph falls back to
the cached inspect ExitCode so non-zero exits surface even without
a Status string. The ATTENTION card uses the same signal.

SSH command output caps at 16 MB. Before, a runaway remote could
balloon memory or pin the parent on a backpressured pipe. The
threaded drain caps each pipe, drains the remainder to a sink and
joins before waiting on the child to prevent the deadlock.

Container exec validates every container ID before spawning ssh,
so future entry points (MCP, jump-bar paste) cannot smuggle a
shell-meta character through. The containers tab paints sooner on
big fleets via a memoized row build keyed on a content fingerprint.

Demo mode ships a podman-edge host (OOM-killed loki container,
empty Status, podman runtime metadata) so the fallback paths are
visible. Visual regression gains two podman detail goldens.

bump no longer disturbs the help and What's New goldens. Reset the theme
in the visual test setup and serialize theme-mutating tests against the
snapshot suite via GLOBAL_TEST_LOCK, ending a flake under narrow cargo
test filters.

fix: run the site build in CI instead of the removed sync check

The site is build-generated now and scripts/site/check-sync.sh was
deleted with the embedded-copy model. ci.yml and ci.sh were still
calling it; point both at scripts/site/build.mjs, matching the site.yml
build job.

feat: search hosts by multiple space-separated terms

The / search and the tag: filter split the query on whitespace and keep only hosts where every term matches, in any field and any order. "web prod" finds hosts matching both even when the words live in different fields. tag= stays an exact single-tag match.

closes #79

feat: renew Vault SSH certs for file browser and container actions

Certificate renewal previously ran only on the connect path (TUI Enter
and `purple <alias>`). Opening the file browser, transferring files or
running a container operation against a host that uses the Vault SSH
secrets engine could fail on an expired certificate.

Add ensure_vault_cert_for_alias, a worker-thread-safe renewal entry point
that loads the provider and SSH config from disk itself and serializes per
alias so concurrent container fetches never sign the same cert twice. Wire
it into the SSH chokepoints: run_snippet (container listing, inspect, logs,
actions and file browser listing), run_scp (file transfer) and both the
standard and tmux container exec paths.

refactor: inject runtime Env for environment and filesystem paths

Resolve environment variables and the ~/.purple and ~/.ssh paths once at the process edge into a typed runtime::Env, then thread it explicitly through App, the CLI handlers and worker threads instead of reading process globals on demand.

This removes the ambient global state that tests had to serialize by hand: the ENV_LOCK mutex, unsafe std::env::set_var calls and the thread-local path overrides (preferences, containers, ssh_keys) are gone. Tests build a sandboxed Env backed by a self-cleaning temp directory instead of mutating or locking shared process state.

The SSH config parser gains parse_with_env so variable expansion resolves against an injected Env rather than the real environment.

Closes #84

feat: pick files with plain Space and a in the file explorer

Plain Space toggles the file under the cursor and plain a toggles every
visible entry, no modifier keys needed. The file explorer now works
cleanly inside tmux and on macOS keyboard-switching setups where Ctrl
chords get intercepted before reaching purple. Ctrl+Space and Ctrl+A
still toggle the same selection for users with the old muscle memory.

Closes #82

refactor: sub-states own their host-keyed cleanup

Each per-host sub-state (ping, vault, tunnel, file_browser_state,
container_state, containers_overview) gains prune_orphans and
migrate_alias methods. App::reload_hosts and
App::migrate_alias_keyed_caches delegate to those instead of
touching sub-state fields directly, so adding a new alias-keyed
cache only requires implementing the contract.

Vault prune logs cert_cache and cert_checks_in_flight drops in
addition to sign_in_flight. New tests cover both the in_flight
HashSets and the entries HashMaps of the inspect and logs caches.

refactor: scope handlers to per-domain App slices

Handlers now take a narrow per-domain slice of App instead of &mut App,
so the compiler rejects any reach into unrelated state (vault, containers,
providers and so on). Whole-App operations that cannot run on a slice are
queued as deferred effects in src/handler/ctx.rs and applied to the full
App after the handler returns.

The discard-unsaved-changes prompt for host, provider, snippet and tunnel
forms now routes through one shared dirty check per form, so it cannot
drift out of sync and silently drop edits as new fields are added.

refactor: finish per-domain slice migration for handlers

bulk_tag_editor now operates on a narrow slice (BulkTagCtx) with the config write split into a slice-scoped apply plus deferred whole-App tails. refactor: inject runtime::Env for all env and path reads

Every production read of process environment variables and filesystem
paths now flows through an injected runtime::Env, captured once at the
process edge in main and threaded explicitly, instead of ad hoc
std::env / dirs::home_dir calls scattered across loaders, providers,
askpass, logging, update and the SSH config parser.

This closes the isolation gap where tests could read or write the real
~/.purple: App construction is now fully sandboxed, and the suite passes
under a clean HOME. Behaviour is unchanged for users.

feat: quote SSH config values so special characters save reliably

The SSH config writer now wraps single-token directive values (HostName,
User, IdentityFile, ProxyJump, CertificateFile) in double quotes when they
contain whitespace or a quote, escaping embedded backslash and quote. The
parser unwraps and unescapes symmetrically, so values with spaces, a "#" or
quotes round-trip exactly instead of being split or truncated on the next
read. Multi-argument directives such as LocalForward stay unquoted.

Every cloud provider now exposes an injectable HTTP base so the production
fetch path (URL construction, auth header, error mapping, pagination and
host mapping) runs end to end against a mock, for all 16 providers including
the signed (AWS, Oracle, OVH) and multi-host (Azure) paths. The Azure
nextLink follow is anchored to the API host so the bearer token cannot leak
to a look-alike host.

Bump to 3.18.5 and add the changelog entry.
fix: balanced right-margin breathing room on every overlay

refactor: lift screen-enum payloads to domain state; dedupe provider sync

The bulk-confirm, snippet flow, container logs, purge stale and vault
sign dialogs no longer carry their data inside Screen variants. The
payload lives next to the rest of the domain state, so opening or
closing an overlay never clones a logs buffer or a list of stack
members.

Vault cert freshness probe throttled to once per 250ms while a vault
host is selected; external signs still surface within a blink and the
per-frame syscall load drops several-fold.

All 16 cloud providers share a Bearer auth header helper and a typed
metadata builder. The previous per-provider boilerplate (88 inline
metadata.push pairs and 10 inline Bearer headers) is replaced.

Recovery hooks: prune_orphans wiping a payload mid-dialog now drops
the user to HostList instead of stranding them on an empty confirm
screen. migrate_alias on rename follows the renamed alias for
pending_sign, pending_bulk_confirm and logs_view.

feat: surface every tab action in the : palette

Type the action name from any tab. Hosts gains sort, group, view-toggle, tag-filter and Ctrl-a select-all. Containers gains exec, logs, restart, stop, refresh-host, fold-host and Ctrl-k stack-restart. The ? Help action is reachable from everywhere. Picking a tunnel or container from the palette fires Enter automatically, matching the one-shot host-connect rhythm.

JumpAction carries a KeyModifiers field so Ctrl-bound shortcuts dispatch correctly. Multi-char queries get a small mode-match nudge so typing sort from the Tunnels tab prefers Tunnels: Sort over Hosts: Sort. 17 dispatch tests cover the new actions, the auto-Enter on tunnel and container hits, and the (key, modifiers) uniqueness contract. feat: group a pattern's SSH directives into per-category cards

Selecting a wildcard pattern now splits its directives into per-purpose cards (Connection, Authentication, Forwarding, Crypto, Keepalive and more) instead of one flat DIRECTIVES card. Each category renders only when the pattern sets it, and unrecognized keywords fall into an OTHER card so nothing is hidden. The demo config gains a pve-* pattern so the panel is covered in --demo and by a visual golden.

feat: wrap host-list navigation top to bottom like the other tabs

Up, down, Page Up and Page Down in the host list now wrap at the edges, matching the Tunnels, Containers and Keys tabs and the in-search behavior. ci: drop magic-nix-cache from the nix flake check job

ci.sh was a 13-gate local-CI script superseded by scripts/precommit.sh (15 gates) and referenced nowhere in the tree. Its only unique gate, the site build, already runs in CI on every push and pull request.

feat: clearer logs with fault-domain tags and a quieter error level

Every logged event in purple.log now carries a fault-domain tag
([external], [config] or [purple]), so a problem can be attributed
to a remote tool, the SSH config or purple itself by grep alone.

The error level is reserved for genuine SSH connection failures.
Routine non-zero exits from remote commands (container list and
actions, file transfer) now log at debug or warn instead of error.

Host deletes, provider syncs, undo, container actions, tunnel
forward add/edit/delete, host add/edit and tag edits now record
what changed, so a support log tells the full story.

The fault-domain tag check runs in CI as well as precommit.

Closes #86

feat: keep one blank line between every host block on save

Provider sync and host import now insert a blank-line separator before
and after each new host block, matching the guarantee add_host already
provided. Hosts pulled in from cloud providers no longer run together.

write() also normalizes the whole file on save: host blocks that were
glued together before purple managed them gain a blank-line separator.
serialize() stays byte-for-byte round-trip faithful, so undo and config
comparisons are unaffected; only the on-disk file is tidied.

A block kept directly under a group-header comment stays glued, since
that grouping is intentional.

feat: keep every provider's hosts grouped under one header

Provider group headers are now resolved through the registry everywhere,
so all 16 providers behave the same. OVHcloud, Leaseweb, i3D.net and
TransIP kept their group header on startup only by coincidence before;
their display name was maintained in a separate list that had drifted.

Group-comment repair derives its known-provider set from the registry
too, so absorbed headers relocate for every provider.

Sync decides whether to write a group header from the same top-level
lookup it uses to place the host, so a newly synced host gets its header
even when the provider's existing hosts live only in an Included file.

Adds a per-provider scenario matrix and startup-cleanup coverage across
all 16 providers.

test: write vault test stubs once to end flaky exec race

The vault SSH tests wrote a fresh mock `vault` / `ssh-keygen` script per
test and exec'd it immediately. Under parallel scheduling a sibling test's
spawn() fork inherits the still-open write fd, so the exec intermittently
fails with ETXTBSY ("text file busy") on Linux. That surfaced as a random
"Failed to run vault CLI" failure in CI.

Write each stub binary exactly once into a shared OnceLock dir and drive
per-test behavior (stdout, stderr, exit code, captured VAULT_ADDR) through
env vars, so no script is ever written while another is exec'd. Route every
sandbox dir through tempfile::tempdir(), replacing the pid+timestamp temp
paths the isolation rule forbids.

feat: split ~/.purple into config, data, state and cache on request

purple's files fall into four categories, following the XDG Base
Directory specification. Each resolves on its own: PURPLE_<CATEGORY>_DIR
when set, else $XDG_<CATEGORY>_HOME/purple when that variable is set to
an absolute path, else ~/.purple. Nothing moves until a variable is set,
so existing setups keep their layout.

Config holds preferences, snippets, providers and themes. Data holds the
signed certificates and the original SSH config backup. State holds
history, recents, the activity and run ledgers, the logs and the askpass
retry markers. Cache holds the container cache and the version check.

The first run with a category outside ~/.purple copies that category's
files into place when the new directory holds none of them yet, all or
nothing per category, with mode 0700 on new directories and file modes
kept. The seed lands before the theme loads and before the log opens.
The legacy tree stays so unsetting the variables rolls back. The startup
banner lists all four directories and purple logs prints the resolved
log path.

A CertificateFile pointing into the resolved certs directory counts as
purple managed alongside the legacy ~/.purple/certs path, so the Keys
tab and the key push picker keep recognizing signed hosts after a move.

Every test that sets the color mode, the theme or the demo flag holds
GLOBAL_TEST_LOCK for its whole run: the what's new render tests, the
demo tests and the containers overview tests join the visual suite on
that lock. The changelog override is an RAII guard that clears on drop,
every acquisition of the shared lock tolerates poison so one failure
stays one failure and the theme tests drop their second mutex.

check-conventions.sh gate 7 rejects a test file that calls a theme,
color mode or demo mutator without naming the shared lock. Gate 8 keeps
runtime::env::Paths the only place that joins .purple.

in a form: the queue waits and drains when they come back.

On a ProxyJump chain ssh names the hop that refused. Only the target's
own refusal opens a dialog, so a jump host's password or host key never
lands on the machine behind it.

A password kept for the session reaches every later listing, transfer
and container command on that host. It travels in the environment of
the ssh child rather than in argv, and it is released only for a hop
the prompt names inside the connection's own chain. A bastion written
as a bare `ProxyJump host` resolves to no hop, so it is refused rather
than answered. Every background run also carries `-o
NumberOfPasswordPrompts=1`, so ssh asks once and arms no retry marker,
which is what let the second ssh of a two-step listing be refused.

Esc during a push signals the ssh process group and returns at once.
The thread already waiting carries out the SIGKILL escalation, so a
slow host holds neither the render loop nor the exit.

Closes #150

fix: keep a password on the host it was typed for

A bastion written as `ProxyCommand` reaches a machine of its own that no
directive names, so purple read the connection as direct. A prompt it could
not place then fell back to the target, and the credential meant for the
target went to the machine in front of it. Both the password typed in the
TUI and a configured source went out that way.

One gate now covers both channels. A prompt is answered when it names a hop
inside this connection's own chain, or when nothing proxies at all. `ssh -G`
answers the route question, so a `Match` block and a directive above the
first `Host` line count as much as a `ProxyJump` does. Where ssh cannot be
asked, a prompt the model cannot place is refused rather than answered on a
route that may be incomplete. The config model resolves `ProxyCommand` the
way ssh does, taking the first value it obtains across the host's own block
and every pattern above it.

ssh builds a `ProxyJump` hop's command from `-l`, `-p`, `-J`, `-F` and `-v`
alone, so `BatchMode` reaches only the ssh purple starts and a bastion asking
for a password wrote its prompt onto the terminal. The hop does inherit the
environment, so every background run wires `SSH_ASKPASS` with
`SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force`, even with nothing to answer with. The terminal
path keeps ssh's own prompt and its retry marker, and the snippet runs that
arm one clear it again.

A queued question waits for the host list search, the tag field, the jump bar
and any confirm already on screen. A server that asks without identifying
itself behind a bastion gets a reason instead of a prompt whose answer would
be held back for the same cause.

`Esc` during a key push and quitting purple return at once: the wait reaches
its escalation instead of parking on a pipe that a `ProxyCommand` outliving
ssh still holds open, and a reaped child sweeps its group.

A host routed through a `ProxyCommand` is left out of the ping sweep, since
a direct probe there measures a machine the connection does not use.
